spec_match.rationale: Value grammar, initial value and applies-to were read from CSSWG PR 14152 rather than inferred: auto | none, initial auto, scroll containers, discrete animation. The support probe rejects invented keywords as well as accepting the real ones, because CSS.supports on a valid value alone cannot distinguish an implemented property from a tolerated declaration.

interactive.rationale: A live grammar prober with a free-text value and a target selector; two instrumented scroll panes that record every scroll event with per-axis deltas; and two maps that draw the scroll path on a canvas and report its straightness.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index says what the property does and, importantly, what auto does not promise — the user agent may lock, so device behaviour varies. Each card matches its page.

edge_cases.rationale: The interesting edge is the one the demos cannot force: axis locking is a compositor decision about a real gesture, and a headless run has no gesture to make. Rather than stage one, the recorder ships a programmatic control that is explicitly labelled as bypassing the gesture pipeline, and every page tells the reader that a finger or trackpad is what exercises the feature.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5908461532610560 on the index and all three concept pages, with CSSWG PR 14152 and CSS Overflow 5.

conformance.rationale: Six immutable assertions: both keywords parse, three invented keywords are rejected, the initial value is auto so adoption is opt-in, the declared value round-trips on a scroll container, and programmatic scrollBy is never axis-locked — the control the recorder demo depends on.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150, twice: flag off (3/3, 24 assertions — every keyword dropped, banner reports the property as unrecognised) and with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features (3/3, 24 assertions — both keywords parse, invented ones rejected, computed values round-trip). Partial rather than pass because the property's actual effect on a gesture was NOT verified: no touch or trackpad input was driven, so these runs prove the declaration is live and the instrumentation is correct, not that locking changed.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert carrying whether the property is supported, the measured event counts, and the measured straightness ratios.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout including the canvas stroke colours, which are read from the custom properties rather than hard-coded; buttons set background and colour; 44px control minimums; the event table scrolls inside its own container.

accessibility.rationale: Both scroll panes are focusable regions with accessible names so they can be scrolled from the keyboard; each canvas carries role=img with a description of what it plots; every verdict is a sentence with the measured numbers in it; results are announced through aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Pane grids are auto-fit minmax and stack at 360px; the canvases are width:100%/height:auto so they scale with the column; overscroll-behavior:contain keeps a pane's scroll from chaining to the page on touch. Mobile is in fact the class where this feature matters most, since touch is where locking is applied.

openQuestions.title: Drive a real touch gesture through CDP and record the result
openQuestions.detail: Input.dispatchTouchEvent produces trusted input, which means a synthesised diagonal swipe would go through the same compositor path a finger does and could settle whether auto actually locks on this platform. That needs the drive harness to gain an input-dispatch primitive; today it only evaluates script in the page, so the recorder's gesture claim rests on the reader's own hand. This is the single most valuable follow-up on this feature.

openQuestions.title: Report which input device produced each recording
openQuestions.detail: A scroll event does not say what caused it, so the recorder cannot distinguish a wheel from a trackpad from a finger — and the three behave differently under auto. Listening for pointerdown/wheel alongside scroll would let each recording be labelled with its likely source, which would stop a mouse-wheel reading being mistaken for evidence that locking does not happen.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive side by side comparison panes without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Auto-fit grids with intrinsic minimums so comparison panes stack rather than squeeze; keep wide tabular content in its own scroll container.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Pane grids use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280–300px, 1fr)) with align-content:start; the seven-column event table sits in an overflow-x:auto scroller because its rows are nowrap by design.

guidanceConsulted.query: keyboard accessible scrollable region with a canvas visualisation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Give scrollable regions a role and an accessible name so they are reachable and operable from the keyboard, and give canvas output a text equivalent.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Every scroll pane is tabindex=0 with role=region and an aria-label naming its configuration; each canvas is role=img with a label, and its content is also reported numerically in the adjacent definition list and verdict sentence.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive scrolls the panes and asserts the verdict text; the numbers in the list are the canvas's own data.

summary: Three concepts around a property whose effect is a gesture decision. The grammar and the plumbing are verified in both flag states; the gesture itself is left to the reader's hand and clearly labelled as such, with a programmatic control included specifically to show what does NOT exercise the feature.
